acceptance-criteria.criterion: When a link is posted with a url and a title, the system shall store it and return 201 with an integer id, the submitted url and title, and a created_at timestamp.
When a link is posted with a url and no title, the system shall store it with a null title and return 201.
If a link is posted with no url field, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.
If a link is posted with a url that does not parse as an absolute http or https URL, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.

context.data-model: Link(id integer pk, url text not null, title text null, created_at timestamp not null)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Save a link (slug: save-link, must-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open.
A POST endpoint that accepts a URL and an optional title, stores it, and returns the stored record including its generated id and creation timestamp.
The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page, because fetching the page would make the endpoint depend on the network.
Considerations (verbatim from the feature): Duplicate URLs are allowed. Deduplication sounds obviously desirable but needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is not worth making for a fixture.
CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS TASK: - The endpoint path is `/links`, UNPREFIXED. Not `/api/links`. Two earlier analysis passes invented an `/api` prefix with nothing in the PRD to read it from; the only path the PRD names verbatim is `GET /links`, and the two write endpoints sit under the same root. - Do NOT deduplicate. Posting the same url twice must create two rows with two different ids and return 201 both times. `Link.url` carries no unique constraint (L1-001), so nothing at the storage layer stops it and nothing in this task may add a check that does. - Do NOT fetch the page to derive a title. The endpoint makes no network call of any kind. A missing title is stored as SQL NULL and reported as JSON `null`.

task.objective:
Create the Pydantic request and response schemas for a link and the `POST /links` route that stores one, so that posting a url with an optional title returns 201 with the stored record, and a request whose url is missing or is not an absolute http or https URL is rejected with 422 having written nothing.
This task also owns `LinkResponse`, the SINGLE response schema every link-returning endpoint in this project uses. L2-002 (`GET /links`) and L2-003 (`POST /links/{id}/tags`) both import it from `app/schemas/link.py` and neither redefines it. It therefore carries the link's tag NAMES as well as its four columns, because tag-links criterion 1 requires the tagging endpoint's response to report every attached tag, and a second response schema for that would make two endpoints disagree about the shape of a link.
This task mounts nothing. It defines an `APIRouter` and leaves it unmounted; L4-001 includes it on the application.

Create the directory `app/schemas/` and the file `app/schemas/link.py` with exactly this content:
"""Pydantic schemas for the link endpoints."""
from datetime import datetime from urllib.parse import urlparse
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
class LinkCreate(BaseModel): """Request body for POST /links."""
url: str title: str | None = None
@field_validator("url") @classmethod def url_must_be_absolute_http(cls, value: str) -> str: """Reject anything that is not an absolute http or https URL.""" parsed = urlparse(value) if parsed.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parsed.netloc: raise ValueError("url must be an absolute http or https URL") return value
class LinkResponse(BaseModel): """One stored link, as returned by every endpoint in this project."""
model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
id: int url: str title: str | None created_at: datetime tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
@field_validator("tags", mode="before") @classmethod def tag_names(cls, value: object) -> object: """Accept a list of Tag rows and report their names.""" if isinstance(value, list): return [item if isinstance(item, str) else item.name for item in value] return value
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- `url: str` with an explicit validator, NOT `pydantic.AnyHttpUrl` and NOT `pydantic.HttpUrl`. Those types NORMALISE the value - `https://example.com` comes back as `https://example.com/` with a trailing slash added - and save-link criterion 1 requires the response to carry "the submitted url". A plain `str` plus a validator rejects the same inputs without rewriting the accepted ones.
- Raising `ValueError` inside a `field_validator` is what produces the 422. FastAPI converts a request-body validation failure into `RequestValidationError`, whose default handler responds 422. Do NOT raise `HTTPException` here and do NOT catch the error in the route: the status code comes for free and hand-rolling it would produce 400.
- The absoluteness test is `parsed.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parsed.netloc`. Both halves are required. The scheme check alone accepts `http://` with no host; the netloc check alone accepts `ftp://example.com`. Together they reject `example.com` (no scheme), `/links/1` (no scheme), `//example.com/a` (no scheme), `ftp://example.com` (wrong scheme) and `http://` (no host), and accept `http://example.com` and `https://example.com/a?b=c#d`.
- `title: str | None = None`. Omitting the key entirely and sending `"title": null` are both legal and both store SQL NULL. Do not make it required and do not default it to the empty string or to any value derived from the url.
- `LinkResponse` sets `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`. That is what lets FastAPI serialise the `Link` ORM instance the route returns. Without it, FastAPI raises a validation error at response time because a `Link` is not a dict.
- `LinkResponse.tags` is `list[str]` - the tag NAMES, not `Tag` objects and not ids - with `default_factory=list` so a link with no tags reports `[]`. The `mode="before"` validator maps each `Tag` row to `item.name` so `LinkResponse.model_validate(link)` works directly on an ORM instance; the `isinstance(item, str)` branch lets the same schema also validate a plain dict, which is what makes it usable in a test assertion. Do NOT import `app.models` into this module - the duck-typed `item.name` keeps the schema layer free of a model import.
- `created_at: datetime`. It serialises to an ISO-8601 string in the JSON body. It is a NAIVE datetime holding UTC (L1-001's decision), so the serialised form carries no offset. Do not add a timezone and do not reformat it.
- Field ORDER in `LinkResponse` is `id, url, title, created_at, tags`. L2-002 and L2-003 assert on this schema's field names; adding, removing or renaming one breaks them.

Create `app/api/save_link.py` with exactly this content:
"""POST /links - store a link with an optional title."""
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.database import get_db from app.models import Link from app.schemas.link import LinkCreate, LinkResponse
router = APIRouter()
@router.post( "/links", response_model=LinkResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED, ) def save_link(payload: LinkCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Link: """Store the posted link and return it with its generated id and timestamp.""" link = Link(url=payload.url, title=payload.title) db.add(link) db.commit() db.refresh(link) return link
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The path is `"/links"`, with NO prefix. Do not write `APIRouter(prefix="/api")`, do not write `"/api/links"`, and do not pass `tags=` or `prefix=` to `APIRouter()`. L4-001 includes this router with a bare `app.include_router(router)`, so whatever path is written here is the path the application serves.
- The module-level name is `router`. L4-001 imports it as `from app.api.save_link import router as save_link_router`. Renaming it breaks a task that cannot see this file.
- `status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED`. FastAPI's default for POST is 200; criteria 1 and 2 both require 201, so the explicit status code is mandatory.
- `db: Session = Depends(get_db)`. Do not construct `SessionLocal()` in the route: the test overrides `get_db`, and a route that ignores it reads a different database.
- `db.refresh(link)` after the commit re-reads the row, which guarantees `id`, `created_at` and the (empty) `tags` collection are populated from storage before the response is serialised. Keep it even though `expire_on_commit=False` makes the attributes readable without it - the refresh is what makes the response provably reflect what was stored.
- The route returns the `Link` ORM instance and lets `response_model=LinkResponse` do the conversion. Do not build a dict by hand: a hand-built dict would drift from the schema L2-002 and L2-003 also use.
- No deduplication. Do not query for an existing row with the same url, and do not return an existing link. The feature states verbatim that duplicate URLs are allowed.
- No network call. Do not fetch the page to derive a title, do not import `httpx`, `requests` or `urllib.request` in this module.
- Do NOT call `app.include_router(...)` and do NOT import `app.main` here. This module defines a router and nothing else.
- Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` anywhere. The test fixture creates the schema for tests and L4-001 creates it for the running application.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/main.py`, `app/database.py`, `app/models/__init__.py`, `app/models/link.py`, `app/models/tag.py`, `app/models/link_tag.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_setup.py`, `tests/test_model_link.py`, `tests/test_model_tag.py`, `tests/test_model_link_tag.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` or `.gitignore`.
Do not create `app/api/list_links.py` or `app/api/tag_links.py` - those are L2-002's and L2-003's files and creating them here would collide in the merge queue. Do not create `app/schemas/tag.py` - that is L2-003's file. Do not create `app/schemas/__init__.py`: it is not needed (see the project-structure note) and the file budget for this task is three.
Do not create a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

# app/schemas/link.py from datetime import datetime
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
class LinkResponse(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
id: int url: str title: str | None created_at: datetime tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
Import as: `from app.schemas.link import LinkResponse`
Downstream contract - THIS IS THE ONE RESPONSE SCHEMA FOR A LINK: - L2-002 (`GET /links`) and L2-003 (`POST /links/{id}/tags`) both import this class. Neither defines its own link response model. A second one would let two endpoints disagree about the shape of a link. - `from_attributes=True` means `response_model=LinkResponse` serialises a `Link` ORM instance directly; a route may `return link` and `return list(links)`. - `tags` is a list of tag NAMES (`list[str]`), never `Tag` objects and never ids. The `mode="before"` validator maps `Tag` rows to `item.name`, so `link.tags` (a `list[Tag]`) converts automatically. The order is whatever `Link.tags` yields - `Tag.id` ascending, which L1-003 made stable - so a test may assert the list without sorting it. - `tags` defaults to `[]`, so a link with nothing attached reports an empty array, never null and never a missing key. - `title` is `str | None`: an untitled link serialises as `"title": null`. The key is always present. L2-002's criterion 3 depends on exactly this. - `created_at` is a naive UTC `datetime` and serialises to an ISO-8601 string with no offset, at microsecond resolution. - Field order is `id, url, title, created_at, tags`. Do not add, remove or rename a field.

Downstream contract: - The request body for `POST /links`. Only that endpoint uses it; L2-003 declares its own request schema for the tagging body. - A missing `url`, or one whose scheme is not `http`/`https` or which has no host, fails validation and FastAPI answers 422 before the route body runs, so nothing is stored. - An accepted url is stored and returned BYTE-FOR-BYTE as submitted. No normalisation, no trailing slash. This is why the field is `str` and not `pydantic.AnyHttpUrl`.
